title: NARUTO SHIPPUDEN: Ultimate Ninja STORM 4
provenance: verified locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro), engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.9.3
notes: Plays on D3DMetal. Tested 2026-09-10 on an M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2: a fight renders and plays correctly at 1920x1080 on D3DMetal, which is what this row now tells Highball to pick. The other two modes do not work for this game and the difference is stark: on DXMT 0.80 the movie, title and menus are fine but in a fight the frame flashes black most of the time with brief moments of the correct image, at a steady 30 fps and 13 ms of GPU; on DXVK 1.10.4 the 2D HUD draws and the 3D world never appears, with a clean log. D3DMetal is Apple's Game Porting Toolkit and is gated on Apple's licence, which Highball asks you to accept the first time a game needs it. Before the first start Steam shows a Bandai Namco licence agreement inside its own window that has to be accepted once. The game is built for a pad and shows pad glyphs: on a keyboard the default mapping is A = L, B = ;, X = K, Y = O, Start = Enter, movement on WASD, so the Press A title screen and the first-run save dialog both want L. Change it in Options > Controls or in config.ini next to the exe. 30 fps is the game's own cap in menus and cinematics.

d3dmetal.detail: fight renders and plays correctly at 1920x1080, confirmed by the maintainer playing it (2026-09-10, r2, macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro). No HUD reading was taken in the fight; menus and cinematics sit at the game's own 30 fps cap.

dxmt.detail: movie, title and menus correct; in a fight the frame flashes black with brief flashes of the correct image, 30 fps, 13 ms GPU (2026-09-10, r2). Not playable.

dxvk.detail: HUD draws, the 3D world is black apart from a few effect sprites, DXVK-Kegworks 1.10.4 log clean (2026-09-10, r2).

verified.fps: plays in a fight on D3DMetal at 1920x1080; 30 in menus and cinematics, the game's own cap. Not measured in the fight.

knownIssues.symptom: On DXMT a fight is black most of the time with brief flashes of the picture; on DXVK the characters and stage never draw.
knownIssues.cause: unknown. The game runs at a steady frame rate and the HUD is fine on both, so it is the 3D scene's presentation that those two modes get wrong.
knownIssues.fix: use D3DMetal, which this row selects for you.
